summary: Two environments, tc-v2 and tc-v3. Each is the unchanged phase-2 interpreter and package set plus FFmpeg 7 shared libraries supplied on LD_LIBRARY_PATH. No Python package is added, removed or upgraded. Because the dynamic-library environment differs, these are distinct environments, not replays of the phase-2/phase-3 environments.

blocker_diagnosis.observed_in_phase3: shifted-queries/2026-11-22/evidence/*_probe.json default_backend_attempt: RuntimeError 'Could not load libtorchcodec' with 'FFmpeg version 7: libavutil.so.59: cannot open shared object file' (and the same for 6/5/4).
blocker_diagnosis.reproduced_2026_11_22: ldd site-packages/torchcodec/libtorchcodec_core7.so in both phase-2 venvs lists libavutil.so.59, libavcodec.so.61, libavformat.so.61, libavdevice.so.61, libavfilter.so.10, libswscale.so.8 and libswresample.so.5 as 'not found'. ldconfig -p lists no libav*/libsw* library. No system ffmpeg binary or library is installed.
blocker_diagnosis.not_the_cause: torch/torchcodec/Python versions. The official torchcodec README table pairs torchcodec 0.5 with torch 2.7 and Python >=3.9,<=3.13; installed: torchcodec 0.5, torch 2.7.1+cpu, Python 3.11.17. The v0.5.0 README states FFmpeg major versions 4 to 7 are supported, and the wheel ships libtorchcodec_core{4,5,6,7}.so only.
blocker_diagnosis.why_pyav_worked: PyAV 15.1.0 bundles its own FFmpeg (libavutil 59.39.100, libavcodec 61.19.101, i.e. FFmpeg 7.1.x) under auditwheel-renamed sonames in site-packages/av.libs/, so pyav never needs system FFmpeg. torchcodec resolves the unrenamed sonames and cannot see them.

torchcodec_readme_tag_v0.5.0.says: TorchCodec supports all major FFmpeg versions in [4, 7]; easy install: conda install ffmpeg (-c conda-forge). Its own table stops at 0.4 (torch 2.7).

compatibility_sources.lerobot_requirement: lerobot-0.3.3 and lerobot-0.4.0 METADATA: Requires-Dist torchcodec<0.6.0,>=0.2.1 (linux x86_64); torch<2.8.0,>=2.2.1. torchcodec 0.5 is inside both ranges.

ffmpeg_provisioning.chosen: Soname aliases pointing at PyAV 15.1.0's bundled FFmpeg 7.1.x libraries inside each phase-2 venv. setup_ffmpeg_aliases.py creates /tmp/kinema-tc-ffmpeg-<env>/ holding seven symlinks named with the sonames libtorchcodec_core7.so requests, after verifying each target's sha256 below. LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<alias dir>:<venv>/site-packages/av.libs (the second entry resolves the targets' own auditwheel-renamed dependencies, which their $ORIGIN rpath looks for next to the alias). Remove with rm -rf /tmp/kinema-tc-ffmpeg-<env>; nothing inside either venv is written.
ffmpeg_provisioning.consequence: Both backends execute the same FFmpeg binaries in the same process. Decoder-library build differences are therefore not a source of pyav/torchcodec differences here; differences come from the backends' own code (frame selection, seeking, colour conversion). A user's system or conda FFmpeg 7 build could still produce different pixels from these.
ffmpeg_provisioning.abi_note: libtorchcodec_core7.so was built against FFmpeg 7.0.1 headers (fetch_and_expose_non_gpl_ffmpeg_libs.cmake at v0.5.0). FFmpeg keeps ABI within a library major version (libavcodec 61, libavutil 59), which is the basis on which torchcodec accepts any FFmpeg 7.x.
